summary: Opaque native addon with credential-search and host-fingerprinting capabilities under an anomalous auto-generated version
details: Package ships a single 10 MB stripped Linux x86_64 Node.js N-API addon as its main entry, with a one-line README that does not describe the binary's purpose. The version string `3.1.41-v2026.217.1-native-tools-392-1785759657` encodes a build counter and a unix timestamp rather than a normal semver release. Binary strings include a full embedded HTTP/TLS client (ureq/rustls), zip handling, SQLite with authentication support (`SQLITE_AUTH_USER`), credential-shaped messages such as `Found login for`, and host/hardware fingerprinting reads against `/dev/disk/by-id/`, `/etc/lsb-release`, `network_adapters`, and `CPU implementer`. The `-linux-x64-gnu` naming mimics the platform-suffix convention used by legitimate prebuilt native addons, but there is no accompanying JavaScript wrapper or umbrella package documenting a purpose, no source, and no API surface exposed to justify a browser-login-database reader, disk-serial enumerator, and outbound HTTP client bundled together. The capability set matches host reconnaissance plus credential harvesting with outbound network delivery; a specific destination URL cannot be recovered from the stripped binary strings alone.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
